## Key accepted decisions

- `DEC-4` Roles as skills before runtime agents — Permanent roles are product concepts/skills/prompts in the MVP, not runtime agents.
- `DEC-5` Sandboxing deferred and optional — Sandboxing is optional and off by default; not an MVP prerequisite.
- `DEC-6` Focus is distinct from lifecycle status — focusWorkItemId names the item receiving attention; it is not a status and does not imply in_progress.
- `DEC-8` Model-generated interpretations are never applied to canonical project truth ... — Model-generated interpretations are never applied to canonical project truth silently; the user reviews an understanding check first.
- `DEC-9` Schema version 3 is introduced with an explicit 2 -> 3 migration (inspect, --... — Schema version 3 is introduced with an explicit 2 -> 3 migration (inspect, --apply, backup, atomic replace).
- `DEC-10` Revision requests are durably recorded before a corrected draft is staged: re... — Revision requests are durably recorded before a corrected draft is staged: reviews.jsonl is append-only, each record uses the defined six fields (intakeId, reviewedRevision, action, optional feedback, timestamp, resultingStatus), and numbered prior drafts and Understanding Checks remain preserved.
- `DEC-11` Product renamed from NewFang to Voila; NF-n IDs remain stable — The active product is named Voila (plain ASCII, never the accented spelling). The command is /voila, model tools use the voila_ prefix, canonical state lives in .voila/, and the Pi adapter is .pi/extensions/voila.ts. The existing NF-n, DEC-n, ASM-n, RSK-n, INT-n, ORI-n, CLM-n, and RCP-n identifier namespaces are NOT renumbered; NF-n is now a stable legacy identifier namespace rather than active branding, and allocation continues in that namespace.
- `DEC-12` Completion requires the tier a criterion actually names, not only a passing suite — NF-1 through NF-4 were completed through the protected gate during the Phase 7 walk-through and then reverted to their prior statuses. They stay held until the tiers their acceptance criteria actually depend on are observed: the interactive Steward Console for NF-1, an authenticated Project Steward intake run for NF-2, and NF-3 as a dependency of NF-4. The claims (CLM-3, CLM-4, CLM-5) and receipts (RCP-5 through RCP-9) produced during the walk-through are real and are retained; the claims now name the tier they do not cover.
- `DEC-13` Extensions-first architecture — Ship Voila as project-local Pi extensions first; package second; SDK/RPC held in reserve. A global install is available via ~/.pi/agent/extensions/ without packaging.
- `DEC-14` Canonical repository state in .voila/ — project.json is authoritative; events.jsonl is append-only history; PROJECT_STATUS.md is generated. Canonical state lives in .voila/; a legacy .newfang/ tree is detected and migrated explicitly, never operated on in place.
- `DEC-15` Thin Pi adapter, modular src/ — .pi/extensions/voila.ts is a thin adapter; domain/state/tools/ui live in src/ and are Pi-free.
- `DEC-16` The language model interprets; Voila owns preservation and enforcement — The language model performs interpretation; Voila owns preservation, schemas, lifecycle, review, application, persistence, provenance, and resumability.

## Open assumptions

- `ASM-1` (medium) The Pi extension/TUI surfaces Voila uses are stable at the pinned 0.82.0.
- `ASM-2` (high) A single primary macOS/Apple Silicon machine is the initial target.
- `ASM-3` (high) Repository-local orientation is sufficient for this phase; no external research is required.

## Open risks

- `RSK-2` (low/high) Single-writer assumption for .voila/ could race under concurrent writers.
- `RSK-3` (medium/low) Terminal UI overload as console modules grow.
- `RSK-4` (medium/medium) Scope creep into project-management ceremony.
- `RSK-5` (medium/medium) Interpretation of planning documents is nondeterministic, so the understanding check and human acceptance are the only guarantees that canonical truth is correct.
